_doc: Rich-output types available to the model in the conversation-system prompt. Each entry contributes one convention block. Loaded via TemplateManager.loadJson(ConfigTemplateId.RichOutputTypes) and rendered by SystemPromptSlot. Register a new type by appending an entry — no code change required unless a new renderer needs UI-side wiring.

_fields.id: Stable slug (kebab-case). Used in tests / logs.
_fields.label: Short display name for logs/docs. Not shown to end users today.
_fields.renderer: 'native' means the plugin renders the block directly (e.g. Mermaid via Streamdown). 'source-only' means the model emits source and the user copies it into a `.ext` file.
_fields.conventionMarkdown: Markdown block appended to the conversation-system prompt. Should describe when to use, the fenced code fence tag, and any structural rules the model must follow.

types.label: Mermaid diagram
types.conventionMarkdown:
Mermaid diagram conventions (when generating mermaid blocks):
- Prefer node labels that reference real vault documents. Wrap document references with double-quoted labels: `A["Note Title"]`.
- To make a node clickable and open the referenced vault note, add a `click` directive with a `peak://wikilink/` URL: `click A "peak://wikilink/Note%20Title" "Open note"`. Use URL-encoding for spaces and special characters.
- Do NOT invent vault paths. Only add `click` directives for notes you know exist (from the current conversation context or attached resources).
- Example:
  ```mermaid
  graph TD
    A["Concept Overview"] --> B["Sub-topic Details"]
    click A "peak://wikilink/Concept%20Overview" "Open Concept Overview"
    click B "peak://wikilink/Sub-topic%20Details" "Open Sub-topic Details"
  ```

types.label: Obsidian Bases view
types.conventionMarkdown:
Obsidian Bases view conventions (when the user asks for a data view / database / Bases file):
- Bases files use extension `.base` and contain YAML with three top-level keys: `filters` (which notes to include), `views` (how to display), and optionally `properties` (per-property display metadata).
- Emit generated Bases in a fenced code block tagged `base`. The chat UI adds a "Save & Open in Bases" button on every `base` block that writes the YAML to a `.base` file and opens it in Obsidian for native rendering.
- **First line of the block should be a filename hint**: `# filename: my-projects.base` (kebab-case, no spaces). If the hint is absent, the file is saved with a timestamped name. The hint is stripped before the file is written.
- Example:
  ```base
  # filename: active-projects.base
  filters:
    and:
      - file.tags.contains("project")
      - status != "archived"
  properties:
    status:
      displayName: Status
    priority:
      displayName: Priority
  views:
    - type: table
      name: Active Projects
      order:
        - file.name
        - status
        - priority
        - file.mtime
      sort:
        - property: priority
          direction: DESC
  ```
- Filter operators: `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `contains(...)`, `startsWith(...)`, `endsWith(...)`, `taggedWith(...)`. Combine with `and:` / `or:` / `not:` blocks.
- Built-in file properties: `file.name`, `file.path`, `file.folder`, `file.ext`, `file.mtime`, `file.ctime`, `file.size`, `file.tags`, `file.links`, `file.inlinks`, `file.outlinks`.
- View types: `table` (columns via `order`), `cards` (`imageProperty` optional), `board` (`groupBy` required), `calendar` (`dateProperty` required).
- Only reference vault properties that exist. If unsure, use `file.*` built-ins.
